cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Every Kubernetes API request clears four sequential gates: Authentication (who are you), Authorization (are you allowed), Admission Control (does cluster policy accept or mutate it), and finally persistence to etcd. Each gate is a separate security and validation filter.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The gates run in strict order and are independent: passing one does not guarantee passing the next. A request rejected at any gate never reaches etcd. Admission control can both mutate and reject objects based on cluster policy.

questions.q: Once a request passes authentication, is it guaranteed to succeed?
questions.a: No. Authentication only establishes identity. The request still must pass authorization and admission control before it is saved.

questions.q: Name the four gates in order.
questions.a: Authentication, Authorization, Admission Control, then persist to etcd.

questions.q: What can admission control do to a request?
questions.a: Evaluate it against cluster policy and either mutate it or reject it.
